acceptanceCriteria: A policy-enabled gate can be satisfied by a recorded green CI run (run id, head sha, conclusion) on a protected intent-branch commit that descends from the attempt candidate, without local execution, and complete accepts it.
Receipt audit verifies the recorded CI source (ancestry from git; run facts as recorded claims) and fails a rewound branch; rollback is a policy flag.
Measured: closing N merged-and-CI-green tickets takes no local make gate runs.
body: Observed 2026-10-21 (build 699): 91 delivered tickets queued for closeout ran close-delivered.sh serially; each required full-gate executed `make gate` locally (1-2 h at load 50-200). After ~80 min only 3 of 91 had completed. Every ticket was already on main via a batch PR whose merge_group/push CI run was green. Owner directed that CI-checked work needs no local gate, so 86 were closed with ticket complete-manual citing a sha256 of a JSON evidence file (lane PR, batch PR, main commit, green CI run URLs); evidence retained in .git/ci-evidence-2026-10-21. complete-manual loses the gate binding and needs per-ticket evidence plumbing. V1-2193 descendant reuse helps only after one local full-gate PASS at a main descendant. Expected: a typed, policy-allowed gate source that records a full-gate PASS from a verified green CI run on a protected-branch commit descending from the candidate (run id, head sha, conclusion), audited like descendant reuse. Actual: COMMAND gates only record local execution or same-tree/descendant local reuse.

title: Gates cannot accept a green merged CI run as evidence: delivered tickets pay a local full-gate each or fall back to complete-manual
